comments.body:
## PRODUCTION-STATE SMOKING GUN — the comment-ID dedup map is EMPTY

Direct inspection of the live binding store on the `tickets` branch
(`git show origin/tickets:.bridge_state/bindings.json`):

```
top-level keys: ['bindings', 'comment_ids', 'reverse', 'version']
bindings entries:      2475
comment_ids ENTRIES:      0     <-- empty
```

**Zero entries**, after thousands of comments have been successfully posted to Jira. The map is
present and structurally valid — it is simply never populated.

### Why that is the whole story

`_diff_comments` (`outbound_comments.py:405-445`) has two skips, and the code is explicit that
the first is PRIMARY and the second is only belt-and-suspenders:

1. **PRIMARY — ID identity:** `binding_store.is_comment_mapped(local_comment_key)`
   (`outbound_comments.py:411-415`). The docstring notes "Identity is the key/ID, NOT the body —
   so same-text comments never collide and an edited body is not seen as new."
   **With `comment_ids` empty this skip can never fire for any comment on any issue.**
2. **SECONDARY — body equality:** `compare_body not in jira_bodies`
   (`outbound_comments.py:439`), described in-code as
   "a SECONDARY (belt-and-suspenders) skip behind the ID identity above — it guards a lost map
   write (a crash between `add_comment` and `record_comment_id`'s save)".

The intended safety net has become the *only* mechanism, and it is inherently lossy: it compares a
locally fitted+normalized body against bodies that have round-tripped through ADF/wiki
conversion. The in-code comment at `outbound_comments.py:433-438` already concedes the rich path
can diverge on trailing whitespace.

**This predicts exactly the per-issue variation observed, and it matches:**

| Jira key | local comments | re-emitted/pass | matched by body | comment character |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| REB-424 | 25 | 3 | 22 | short/simple |
| REB-1570 | 25 | 8 | 17 | mixed |
| REB-1580 | 24 | 21 | 3 | rich |
| REB-1861 | 40 | 39 | **1** | richest — avg 3.6 KB, heavy markdown |

Rich bodies fail the string-membership test and are re-posted forever; simple ones happen to match.
No uniform "first N comments" pattern fits this data, which rules out a pagination/truncation
explanation — and independently, the bug-1f3d pagination fix **is** present and correct
(`acli_cli_ops.py:583-600` `get_comments` uses `--paginate`; `_parse_paginated_comments` handles
the multi-object stream; the snapshot truncation guard is at `outbound_comments.py:322-346`).

### Relationship to the previously-fixed bug 1f3d-cb66-d3fc-4356

`1f3d` (`florid-vigorous-urial`, closed) fixed the *pagination* route to this same 5000-comment
inflation, and its cleanup task `bd80-0603-7d44-4d9f` purged duplicates from the 13 issues it had
capped. **This is the same failure class arriving through a different route** — the ID-map route —
not a regression of the pagination fix. Notably, `1f3d`'s fix hardened the SECONDARY skip's inputs
while the PRIMARY skip was silently inert the whole time.

### Remaining unknown — do NOT fix from static reading

`comment_ids` is empty because `_record_comment_id`
(`dispatch_apply_phases.py:309-334`) silently returns on any of four guards:
`binding_store is None`; the entry has no `local_comment_key`; the `add_comment` result has no
`id`; or the store lacks `record_comment_id`. Every one is a silent no-op by design, so nothing
reports which fires. A fifth possibility is that `record_comment_id` writes but the map is never
persisted/committed back to `.bridge_state/bindings.json`.

**Which one it is must be established by instrumenting a live pass**, per this ticket's ACs. The
empty map is proof the primary skip is inert; it is not yet proof of which guard causes it.

### Precedent for the duplicate cleanup

`bd80-0603-7d44-4d9f` is the established pattern for purging the duplicates once the loop is fixed
— relevant for REB-1861's ~5000 and the other 27 affected issues.

comments.body:
## ROOT CAUSE CONFIRMED AT RUNTIME — GUARD 3 fires: ACLI returns no top-level `id`

AC 1 satisfied. The failing dedup layer is the PRIMARY (ID-identity) skip, and the specific
guard is the **third** one in `_record_comment_id`
(`dispatch_apply_phases.py:328-330`):

```python
comment_id = add_comment_result.get("id") if isinstance(add_comment_result, dict) else None
if not comment_id:
    return          # <-- silent no-op on EVERY successful Cloud post
```

`add_comment` on the Cloud/ACLI transport does **not** return a comment resource. It returns
ACLI's **batch mutation envelope**, which has no top-level `id` at all.

### Runtime evidence

**(a) The real ACLI envelope, observed live** (`acli 1.3.19-stable`, authenticated against
`navasage.atlassian.net`). Non-mutating probe against a key that cannot exist, so nothing was
created in Jira:

```
$ acli jira workitem comment create --key ZZNOPE-424242 --body "..." --json
{
  "results": [
    { "status": "FAILURE",
      "message": "Issue does not exist or you do not have permission to see it.",
      "id": "ZZNOPE-424242" }
  ],
  "totalCount": 1,
  "successCount": 1
}
```

Note `results[].id` is the **work item key**, not a comment id — ACLI's comment-create is
batch-shaped (`--key` takes a LIST, plus `--jql`/`--filter`), so it reports per-work-item
results and never echoes the created comment resource. This is the same envelope the repo
already documents for the `comment` verb in `AcliMutationError`
(`adapters/jira/acli_subprocess.py:258-276`, bug 44de).

**(b) The guard firing, observed executing.** `_record_comment_id` was instrumented
(`DEBUG-rebar-debug`, since reverted) and driven through the REAL production code — real
`acli_cli_ops.add_comment`, real `subprocess` via `_run_acli`, real `BindingStore`. The only
substitution was the `acli` binary itself, emitting the envelope shape verified in (a):

```
DEBUG-rebar-debug GUARD-3 no-id result={'results': [{'status': 'SUCCESS', 'message': 'Comment added',
                                         'id': 'REB-1861'}], 'totalCount': 1, 'successCount': 1}
add_comment returned top-level .get('id') -> None
comment_ids -> {}
is_comment_mapped(key) -> False

CONTROL (the shape the tests assume, {"id": "10001"}):
DEBUG-rebar-debug RECORDED key=1787251802516868001 id=10001
comment_ids -> {"1787251802516868001": "10001"}
```

The control proves guards 1, 2 and 4 and the persistence path are all healthy — the same call
with an id-bearing result records and saves.

### The other four candidates, each ruled out

| # | Candidate guard | Verdict | Evidence |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `binding_store is None` | RULED OUT | Threaded end-to-end: `reconcile.py:281` load -> `reconcile.py:526-548` -> `applier.py:488-495` -> `applier.py:641-646` ctx -> `apply_handlers.py:347-355` / `:140-148` -> `dispatch_one.py:475-477` / `:383`. No hop relies on the `None` default. Control run above records successfully. |
| 2 | no `local_comment_key` | RULED OUT **at runtime** | Real production comment record for this very ticket (keys `author/author_email/author_id/body/timestamp`, `timestamp=1787251802516868001`) driven through the REAL `_diff_comments` emits 1 mutation carrying `local_comment_key -> 1787251802516868001`. |
| 3 | `add_comment` result has no `id` | **CONFIRMED** | (a) + (b) above. |
| 4 | store lacks `record_comment_id` | RULED OUT | `BindingStore.record_comment_id` exists (`binding_store.py:359`); control run recorded through it. `_EmptyBindings` is only used on the read-only `reconcile_check` path. |
| 5 | written but never persisted | RULED OUT | `record_comment_id` saves IMMEDIATELY (`binding_lifecycle.py:496-497`); `BindingRepository.save()` writes the whole `_data` atomically (`binding_repository.py:262-279`), `comment_ids` is a top-level template key (`binding_repository.py:56-61`), and the workflow commits `.bridge_state/bindings.json` back (`reconcile.py:665-673`, `_store/push.py:428`). 2475 `bindings` entries prove the write path works. |

Guards 1/2/4/5 are all empirically healthy, yet production `comment_ids` holds **0** entries
after thousands of successful posts. By elimination that is only possible if guard 3 fires on
the success path — i.e. the success payload also lacks a top-level `id`, exactly as the batch
envelope in (a) implies.

### Why the symptom looked body-shaped

With the PRIMARY skip inert, the SECONDARY body-equality skip is the only one left, and it is
lossy by construction (local fitted+normalized body vs. a body that round-tripped through
ADF/wiki). That is why the re-emission rate tracks comment richness (REB-1861 1/40 matched,
REB-424 22/25) rather than any positional pattern. One cause explains every observed symptom.

### Transport asymmetry — why every test passed

The DC/REST transport genuinely does return `{"id": ...}`
(`adapters/jira_datacenter/_links.py:82-84` -> `_unwrap` -> `Comment.raw` from
`POST /rest/api/2/issue/{key}/comment`). Only the **Cloud/ACLI CLI** path is broken. Every
test double asserts the id-bearing shape by assumption — `test_comment_id_capture.py:52,67,81`
(`MagicMock`), and `test_acli_comment_adf_encode.py:32-33`, the one test that stubs actual acli
stdout, hand-invents `'{"id": "10001"}'`. No recorded real comment-create payload exists
anywhere in the repo. Note also that `add_comment` (`acli_cli_ops.py:528-529`) is the ONLY
`--json` consumer in that module that skips the normalizing idiom every sibling uses
(`_parse_acli_comments`, `_parse_paginated_comments`, `get_issue`, `_verify_created_issue`).

### Defect attribution — `caused_by` 789c-1251-fc21-4cf6 (emersed-specific-mutt)

`git blame -w -C -M -L 323,332 dispatch_apply_phases.py` -> **27b868ba55** ("Append-only comment
sync with comment-ID map", `rebar-ticket: 789c-1251-fc21-4cf6`), which introduced
`_record_comment_id` and every one of its guards. That commit is the origin, not merely a
carrier: it added a NEW consumer written against a producer contract it never verified. Ticket
789c's own plan states "an unmapped key is created in Jira and **its returned ID recorded**" —
the Cloud transport never returned one. `acli_cli_ops.add_comment` predates the change and was
correct-at-the-time (nothing read its return value until 789c did), so this is not the
fix-site/cause-site trap: the obligation and the failing consumer were created by the same
commit.

Divergence note: a whole-file blame majority would name the same commit here, so the considered
attribution and the mechanical one agree.

Close class: **`plan_defect`** — the plan's central assumption about the transport contract was
wrong, so the feature shipped inert rather than regressing something that worked. Before 789c
there was no ID dedup at all; 789c promised it and delivered a silent no-op on Cloud.

### Legitimacy: `defect`

Cited authority: ticket 789c's acceptance criteria; the in-code contract on
`BindingLifecycle.record_comment_id` ("the durable entry is what the outbound differ's PRIMARY
skip keys on, so a crash after the Jira post cannot re-post"); and existing tests
(`test_comment_id_capture.py`) that assert the map IS populated after a post. Observed
behaviour contradicts all three.

### Caller-dependency sweep

Post-fix behaviour: `comment_ids` gains an entry per successfully-posted comment, so
`is_comment_mapped` returns True and the PRIMARY skip engages. The map's only PRODUCTION
consumer is `is_comment_mapped` at `outbound_comments.py:414`; `comment_id_for` has **no**
production caller at all (tests only). Nothing depends on the map staying empty. Gate clear.

### Not in scope here

Bug 1f3d (`florid-vigorous-urial`) fixed the *pagination* route to the same 5000-comment
inflation; that fix is present and correct (`acli_cli_ops.py:583-600` `--paginate`, truncation
guard at `outbound_comments.py:322-346`) and is untouched. Cleanup of already-posted duplicates
remains a separate workstream (precedent: `bd80-0603-7d44-4d9f`).

comments.body:
## FIX LANDED FOR REVIEW — Gerrit change 1957

`Record mirrored comments without a Jira id` — https://rebar.solutions.navateam.com/c/rebar/+/1957

### The fix

`_record_comment_id` (`dispatch_apply_phases.py`) no longer makes the durable recording
conditional on the transport echoing a comment id. Reaching that function already means the
post landed — it is only ever called on an `add_comment` that returned without raising, and
ACLI failures raise `AcliMutationError` first. So the `local_comment_key` is now recorded on
every successful post:

```python
-    if not comment_id:
-        return
     recorder = getattr(binding_store, "record_comment_id", None)
     if recorder is not None:
-        recorder(key, comment_id)
+        recorder(key, comment_id or UNKNOWN_COMMENT_ID)
```

A transport-supplied id (DC/REST) is still stored **verbatim** — unchanged behaviour. When the
transport structurally cannot report one (Cloud/ACLI), a named sentinel
`UNKNOWN_COMMENT_ID = "__rebar_unknown_comment_id__"` is stored instead. It is deliberately not
id-shaped, and the work item key from `results[].id` is never stored in its place. The
docstrings on `BindingLifecycle.record_comment_id` / `comment_id_for` and their `BindingStore`
delegates were corrected so the code no longer claims the map always holds a Jira comment id.

The other four guards (no store, entry not a dict, no `local_comment_key`, store predates
`record_comment_id`) are untouched and remain silent no-ops.

4 files, +214/-19. Only `is_comment_mapped` reads this map in production, so the sentinel
changes no behaviour beyond restoring the PRIMARY skip.

### RED -> GREEN

`tests/unit/rebar_reconciler/apply/test_comment_id_acli_envelope.py` (new).

- Seen **RED first**, for the right reason: 3 tests failed on the mechanism (key not recorded /
  not persisted / comment re-emitted); the 4th — the DC-id-verbatim control — passed before and
  after, so the fix is pinned on both sides.
- **Held out** from the implementing subagent: the file was moved out of the worktree entirely
  and the path declared off-limits. The fixer got only the frozen contract, never the
  assertions. It came back GREEN 4/4 against an oracle it had never seen.
- **Mutation check**: re-introducing the exact confirmed root cause (`if not comment_id:
  return`) returned it to RED 3/4; restoring the fix returned it to GREEN. The test has teeth.
- The decisive case is
  `test_no_reemission_after_an_acli_post_even_when_the_body_diverges`: the Jira-side body is
  deliberately made to NOT string-match the local one, so the SECONDARY body-equality skip
  cannot save it — it passes only when the PRIMARY id-identity skip engages.

### Replication of the original report (ACs 2 and 3)

Simulated REB-1861 exactly — 40 rich markdown comments whose bodies diverge through
ADF/wiki round-tripping — driving the REAL enactment site
(`_update_one_dispatch_comments`) with a client returning the REAL ACLI envelope, then
re-running the REAL differ:

```
PRE-FIX                                   POST-FIX
pass 1: pending=40 applied=40  (40 total)  pass 1: pending=40 applied=40  (40 total)
pass 2: pending=40 applied=40  (80 total)  pass 2: pending= 0 applied= 0  (40 total)
pass 3: pending=40 applied=40 (120 total)  pass 3: pending= 0 applied= 0  (40 total)
comment_ids entries: 0                     comment_ids entries: 40
```

AC 2 (a pass over an unchanged ticket computes 0 pending) and AC 3 (two consecutive passes post
0 comments) both satisfied. AC 4's regression test is the held-out suite above, including the
round-trip-transformed body case it explicitly names.

### Sibling sweep (both axes)

**Construct axis — no live siblings.** The class is "a durable record is silently skipped when
an optional-looking field is absent from a transport result". The only two other `.get("id")`
readers of a mutation result both handle absence correctly and are NOT siblings:
`_confirm_link_add` (`dispatch_apply_phases.py:572`) records `link_id=None` and proceeds — it
never skips the recording; `access_check.py:130` reports `no_key_in_response` and fails
**loudly**. Every other ACLI mutation wrapper (`update_priority`, label add, delete) discards
its return entirely, and `create_issue` verifies loudly via `_verify_created_issue`.

**Parity axis — no MISSING slots.** Rule: *a successfully posted outbound comment must be
recorded as mirrored.* Census of the five surfaces:

| Surface | Verdict |
|---|---|
| CLI command | N/A — comment posting is not a user-invoked op; it exists only inside a reconcile pass |
| MCP / API tool | N/A — no MCP tool posts to Jira |
| Library facade | N/A — not on the public `import rebar` surface |
| Automated callers | BOTH enactment sites — `create_one` (`dispatch_one.py:383`) and `_update_one_dispatch_comments` (`dispatch_apply_phases.py:377`) — route through the shared `_record_comment_id`, so one change covers both and they cannot drift. The typed-dispatch leaf (`apply_outbound.py:161-163`) reaches the same helper. Covered. |
| Dual-direction | N/A — inbound (Jira->rebar) mirroring dedups on the local entry's `jira_comment_id` (bug 85a1), a separate mechanism; `is_comment_mapped` is outbound-only. Append-only means there is no outbound comment EDIT path (`acli_graph.update_comment` has no reconciler caller). |

### Fix-safety audit

- **Restoration, not creation** — restores the dedup ticket 789c specified and shipped inert.
  No new entry point, artifact, or mutating external call.
- **No new dependency.**
- **No test weakened** — no pre-existing test file was modified at all (4 files: 3 source, 1 new
  test). `tests/unit/rebar_reconciler` + `tests/integration/rebar_reconciler`: 3015 passed.
- **Not a change-detector** — assertions are on observable output (the map's answer, the
  differ's emitted mutations), not on private names or source text.
- The bug-1f3d pagination fix and the snapshot truncation guard are untouched and verified
  intact.

### Gates

`make lint` All checks passed (incl. `check_complexity_baseline.py --check`:
**new=0 increased=0 stale=0**), `make typecheck` clean over 598 files, all three touched files
well under the 800-LOC cap (532 / 580 / 684). Commit carries the `rebar-ticket:` trailer
(`verify-commit-ticket` OK) and a DCO sign-off.

### Residual risk

1. **The map can no longer supply a real comment id on Cloud.** `comment_id_for` has no
   production consumer today, so nothing breaks — but a future feature needing a real Jira
   comment id (e.g. comment edit/delete mirroring, which append-only currently forbids) would
   have to fetch it. Documented at the sentinel and in both docstrings. **Accepted** — closing
   it would cost an extra `get_comments` call per posted comment for a capability nothing uses.
2. **`add_comment` is the only `--json` consumer in `acli_cli_ops` that skips the normalizing
   idiom its siblings use** (`_parse_acli_comments`, `_parse_paginated_comments`, `get_issue`,
   `_verify_created_issue` all normalize or verify). It returns raw `json.loads(stdout)` to a
   caller typed as returning a comment resource. That mismatch is what let this ship. **Ticket
   filed** — see the follow-up linked `discovered_from` this bug.
3. **No recorded real ACLI payload exists anywhere in the repo**; every double hand-invents the
   shape, which is precisely why this passed every test on both transports. Covered by the same
   follow-up ticket.
4. **The workflow remains disabled** (`reconcile-bridge.yml`). Re-enabling is the operator's
   call once 1957 lands. Duplicate cleanup for REB-1861 (~5000) and the other 27 issues stays a
   separate workstream (precedent `bd80-0603-7d44-4d9f`).

Awaiting `LLM-Review +1` and `Verified +1` before Submit. The ticket will be closed only after
the change merges, with `--class=plan_defect --caused-by=789c-1251-fc21-4cf6`.

comments.body: Residual-risk follow-up filed: **crusty-brinish-ass** (`3235-8aaf-e288-48f2`), linked `discovered_from` this bug — covers the raw-passthrough seam in `acli_cli_ops.add_comment` and the absence of any recorded real ACLI payload fixture, both of which are why this defect passed every test on both transports.

compiled_state.description:
## Summary

The outbound comment sync is **not idempotent**. Comments that have already been posted to Jira
are re-posted on every hourly reconcile pass. Measured on run 32398224961 (2026-08-20T17:33Z):
**205 comments re-posted in a single pass across 28 issues** — roughly **4,920 duplicate Jira
comments per day** at the hourly cadence.

Discovered while root-causing `grievous-vulgar-sanderling` (bug 64a0-8768-038c-45b2), the
heartbeat-canary alarm for reconcile-bridge.yml. That workflow's failure is a downstream
consequence: REB-1861 accumulated duplicates until it hit Jira's hard cap of 5000 comments per
issue, after which every `add_comment` for it fails and reds the run.

## Reproduction Steps

Compare per-issue comment counts across two reconcile-bridge runs several passes apart, for
**closed** tickets with no new local comments:

1. Pull the run logs for two passes (e.g. runs 32344687307 at 07:35Z and 32398224961 at 17:33Z).
2. Grep `RECON: outbound_update key=<KEY> ... comments=<N>` and
   `RECON: batch_outcome ... key=<KEY> ... comments_applied=<M>`.
3. Observe N and M are identical across both passes, and M == N (they land every time).

## Expected vs Actual

- **Expected:** after a comment has landed in Jira, subsequent passes compute 0 pending comments
  for it. A closed ticket with no new local comments converges to `comments=0`.
- **Actual:** the same comments are recomputed as pending and re-posted on every pass, forever.

Evidence (10 passes apart, all closed tickets):

| Jira key | local ticket | local comments | pending 07:35 | pending 17:33 | applied 07:35 | applied 17:33 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| REB-1580 | adroit-deductible-kakapo | 24 | 21 | 21 | 21 | 21 |
| REB-1570 | fireless-schematic-gadwall | 25 | 8 | 8 | 8 | 8 |
| REB-424 | orb-mantle-talon | 25 | 3 | 3 | 3 | 3 |
| REB-1861 | nonmystic-topiary-toadfish | 40 | 39 | 39 | 7 (then capped) | 0 (capped) |

REB-1861 holds **5000** comments in Jira against **40** locally — a 125x divergence produced
entirely by this loop.

## Suspected mechanism (NOT yet confirmed at runtime)

Two layers should independently prevent a re-post; both appear to be failing:

1. **PRIMARY — comment-id dedup.** `_record_comment_id`
   (`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/dispatch_apply_phases.py:309-334`, `emersed-specific-mutt`)
   persists the Jira comment id against the local COMMENT event's HLC so a re-sync skips it. It is
   guarded to be a **silent no-op** in four cases: `binding_store is None`, the entry carries no
   `local_comment_key`, the `add_comment` result carries no `id`, or the store predates
   `record_comment_id`. If any holds in production the primary skip never engages and nothing
   reports that it did not.
2. **FALLBACK — body-membership test.** `_diff_comments`
   (`src/rebar/_engine/rebar_reconciler/outbound_differ.py:707`) treats a comment as needing to be
   added when the local body is not present in the Jira body set. Comments round-trip through
   ADF/wiki-text conversion, so a landed comment's Jira body may never string-match the local body.

Confirming which guard fires requires instrumenting a live pass — that is the first task here.

## Acceptance Criteria

- [ ] Runtime evidence identifying which dedup layer fails (do not fix from static reading alone).
- [ ] A reconcile pass over an unchanged closed ticket computes **0** pending comments.
- [ ] Two consecutive passes with no local changes post **0** comments to Jira.
- [ ] Regression test pinning idempotency: apply a comment, re-run the differ against the resulting
      Jira state, assert no re-emission — including for a body that is transformed on round-trip.
- [ ] Decide and document the remediation for the ~5000 duplicate comments already in REB-1861 and
      the duplicates in the other 27 affected issues (operator decision; may be out of scope here).

## Notes

- Jira's per-issue cap is 5000 comments (`COMMENTS_PER_ISSUE_LIMIT_EXCEEDED`). REB-1580 at
  21/pass reaches it in roughly ten days, at which point it reds the bridge the same way REB-1861
  does now. This is progressive.
- A separate hardening item (worth its own ticket): rebar classifies the permanent cap refusal as a
  per-mutation failure, contrary to the project's documented skip-vs-failure split (ticket a3fa,
  `pass_io.record_capability_gap`) and the hierarchy-rejection precedent
  (`dispatch_one.py:525-558`). That is what converts the cap into a red workflow.
compiled_state.title: Outbound comment sync is not idempotent — ~205 comments re-posted to Jira every hourly pass
